task: On top of PR #575, closed the codemie-code profile-scope gaps. Local config writes now go through a fill/refuse classifier. Setup Local save merges into the existing file. New files and delete repair write activeProfile "". A one-time TTY-gated fallback warning was added, rename is scope-aware, and profile/auth command errors are visible. Code-review fix-ups added a global-config write guard, routed local migrations through the safe read path, and treated inquirer Ctrl+C as a cancel.

component_scope.label: XL
component_scope.affected: ConfigLoader (src/utils/config.ts: local/global write classifier and guard, switch/delete/rename/initProjectConfig, fallback warning, loadLocalMultiProviderConfig used by migrations), profile CLI commands (index.ts, auth.ts, new command-error.ts helper), setup command (Local save merge), AgentCLI (opt-in for the fallback warning), project-config usage guide
component_scope.layers: Service, Workflow (CLI commands), DB-Persistence (config file write/read semantics), Agent-Tool

requirements_clarity.label: M
requirements_clarity.gaps: The spec covered the local write path but missed equivalent hazards on the global write path and in local config migrations. Code review caught both (CR-005, CR-006), as well as inquirer Ctrl+C cancel handling (CR-002..CR-004). The guide's claim that profile names are unique across the system was wrong while unique-name enforcement (PR #585) is still open, so the docs were corrected in CR-001.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: There is no exact precedent for the fill/refuse classifier, which decides whether to fill a partial config file or refuse to touch an unreadable one (null profile entries, a non-string activeProfile, an unknown version, unparseable JSON, a UTF-8 BOM). The write semantics changed on the ConfigLoader path that every agent launch uses. Data loss was a real risk: review found 2 critical issues, a global config overwrite after the stricter guard and migrations overwriting unparseable local files. The one-time fallback warning has to stay TTY-gated so it does not leak into ACP stdio or agent TUIs.
technical_risk.mitigation: Unreadable files are refused and left byte-identical. A real-filesystem test suite (config-local-write.test.ts, 618 lines) uses parameterized malformed-file tables for both the global and local scopes, plus a migration 004 regression test. All 6 blocking review findings were fixed in one round. No schema change and no data migration, so rollback is a normal CLI release.

key_reasoning.reason: Base M (3). The work is concentrated in ConfigLoader plus the profile and setup CLI commands. AgentCLI is a one-line opt-in, and command-error.ts is a helper inside the profile CLI. Two scope red flags raise it to XL. ConfigLoader is a core shared utility on every agent launch path. The changes also reach several workflows: profile switch/rename/delete/status/login/refresh, setup Local save, agent-launch fallback warning, and the local config migrations (via loadLocalMultiProviderConfig). This matches the initial assessment and the project's profile-provider-decoupling calibration example (XL).

Raised from M to L. The fill/refuse classifier and the global write guard are new defensive patterns with no exact precedent, and they changed write semantics on the shared ConfigLoader path. The data-loss risk was real, not theoretical: code review found 2 critical issues (global overwrite after the stricter guard, migrations overwriting unparseable local files) among 6 blocking findings. Fixing them took a second commit round (CR-001..CR-006).

The implementation slice df790403~1..62c45617 changed 10 files (8 modified, 2 new) across 5 directories, with 1155 insertions and 106 deletions. src/utils/config.ts alone was +345 lines and the new config-local-write.test.ts is 618 lines. This lands in the 7-10 file L band, as the initial 8-10 estimate predicted. The full branch diff against 173b148e shows 12 files, but src/env/types.ts and config-project-override.test.ts come only from PR #575 and are excluded.

Raised from M to L. Four distinct layers changed. Service: ConfigLoader logic. Workflow: the profile and setup CLI commands. DB-Persistence: read/write semantics of the global and local config files, including the read path the local migrations use. Agent-Tool: AgentCLI enables the fallback warning. There is no schema change and no new data migration, so it does not reach XL.
